page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What colostrum is
steps.why: A newborn cannot yet make its own antibodies, so it has to be given ready-made ones.
common_mistakes: Describing colostrum as ordinary milk. It is the first milk after delivery.
steps.memory_tip: The first milk carries ready-made IgA antibodies.
steps.margin_note: Define it, then name the antibody.

It has plenty of IgA antibodies, which

steps.label: Why it protects
steps.why: Antibodies made by someone else give immediate protection, but only until they are used up.
common_mistakes: Calling it active immunity. Ready-made antibodies give passive immunity.
steps.memory_tip: The baby receives antibodies, so the immunity is passive and natural.
steps.margin_note: Name the kind of immunity. That is the second mark.

insider_note: Name the antibody: IgA. An answer that says only 'the first milk is good for the baby' has justified nothing.
